note: From the strictly positive reflected two-point value, `scanner_inj` proves full rank (injectivity) for every basis and every pair x ≠ y. That is more general than [M]'s rows at perturbed generic points, and needs neither the perturbation nor the greedy lowering of the kernel dimension.

snippet.text:
theorem scanner_inj (d : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis ι ℂ (W d)) (x y : E4) (hx : x≠y) :
    Injective (fun v : W d => fun i => readsTwo F d x y v (b i)) := by
  intro v w he
  by_contra h
  let B := readsTwo F d x y
  have hz : B v = B w := b.ext (fun i => congr_fun he i)
  have hp := faceTest_eq F d x y (v-w) (v-w)
  have he : 0 < duplex x y (writes F d (v-w)) (writes F d (v-w)) :=
    (reflected_positive hx _).2 (by rw [map_sub]; exact sub_ne_zero.mpr ((writes_inj F d).ne h))
  change B (v-w) _ = _ at hp
  rw [map_sub,hz,sub_self] at hp
  rw [← hp] at he; simp at he

proof_context.conclusion: For every basis `b` and pair `x != y`, `v -> (readsTwo x y v (b i))_i` is injective, using `reflected_positive` for strict positivity of the reflected two-point value.

def vane (B : RStage F d) (x y : E4) (he : couple x y∈generic _) : Cells.Columns C S d where
  dim := B.m
  H := table_spin C.labels
  basis := B.b
  realBasis := B.real_i
  initial := B.unit_
  amount := B.m+1
  row i := colPair _ i x y he
  full := by
    let z (i : Fin (B.m+1)) := colPair _ i x y he
    have hc (p) (i) : (z i).tests (freeTable F) B.b p=readsTwo F d x y p (B.b i) := by
      rw [scan_used]; apply congr_arg ((freeTable F).useAt (freeTable F) (couple x y)); ext1 j; fin_cases j <;> rfl
    change Injective fun p i => (z i).tests (freeTable F) B.b p
    simp_rw [hc]; exact scanner_inj F d B.b x y (pair_ne _ _ (generic_conf _ he))

proof_context.conclusion: The readings at a generic pair `couple x y` form a finite row system whose injectivity is `scanner_inj`.
